windows.reason: The obstacle is the Windows toolchain, not the GPU: on a TheRock Windows build torch::cuda::is_available() returns false inside a standalone C++ executable because the CUDAHooksRegistry entry in torch_hip.dll is never registered, so no AMD card can run the tests there. Determined on windows-gfx1101 and confirmed host-wide on windows-gfx1201. Linux wave64 (gfx90a) and wave32 (gfx1100) both validated at head.
windows.refused_note: Not a platform obstacle -- a build issue that was not explored far enough. The port itself works on Windows: 320/914 tests pass on real gfx1101 including the custom HIP reduction kernels, and the GPU is fully visible (torch._C._cuda_getDeviceCount() > 0 via the ctypes path). All 564 failures fail at ASSERT_TRUE(torch::cuda::is_available()) in the harness before reaching any ported code, because lld-link omits .CRT from torch_hip.dll so REGISTER_CUDA_HOOKS static initializers never run. That is a fixable defect in TheRock's PyTorch Windows build, not a property of Windows, and notes.md itself says a TheRock fix would take this to completed. Investigate before asking again: file the TheRock defect (now in data/deferred.json); try forcing the registration (/WHOLEARCHIVE or a reference into the hooks TU, or _initterm on the DLL CRT section directly); and try running a thread after load, since notes.md records TLS callbacks at known RVAs that fire on DLL_THREAD_ATTACH. None of those was tried.

windows-gfx1101.blocked_reason: torch::cuda::is_available() returns false in standalone C++ exe on Windows TheRock build: CUDAHooksRegistry stays empty because torch_hip.dll REGISTER_CUDA_HOOKS global constructors do not run via PE loader (lld-link omits .CRT$XCU table; _DllMainCRTStartup CRT init ptr is null; TLS callbacks fire only on thread-attach, not process-attach). Native HIP kernel tests 320/914 pass on real gfx1101 GPU (hipGetDeviceCount=1 confirmed); 564 tests fail because each guards on torch::cuda::is_available(); 30 are skipped for same reason. Torch parity oracle and tensor creation tests all require is_available()=true. Cannot fix without rebuilding torch_hip.dll with MSVC link.exe or explicitly registering CUDAHooks at exe startup.

windows-gfx1201.blocked_reason: Host-wide block, GPU-independent (carried from windows-gfx1101 determination): TheRock Windows torch_hip.dll (lld-link, no .CRT$XCU) leaves torch::cuda::is_available()==false in the standalone C++ test exe; native HIP kernels pass but torch-gated tests cannot run. Host toolchain bug, identical on gfx1201.
